item.title: Jerry Jones gives emotional tribute to Martha Firestone Ford
item.description: DETROIT — Among the many tributes to longtime Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford, legendary Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones shared a touching personal story the day after her death at 101 . Jones recalled a trip to Detroit in the early 2000s during the country's financial crisis, which rocked the automobile industry. Ford famously declined a bailout from the U.S. government, but it still was a tough time for the company. "I'll never forget her, her eyes were teared up, seriously," Jones said Wednesday, Nov. 25, on NFL Network's "Good Morning Football. "I remember her talking about what a hard time it had been. The Ford family had taken all of their stock to the bank to borrow money to keep Ford going during a hard time in this country and a hard time in the automobile business. "And I'll never forget her talking about the rough time it was for her, the disappointing time, because the team wasn't playing well, and how special Detroit is." The Lions announced the death of Firestone Ford on Tuesday night, Nov. 24. A member of the famous Firestone (tires) family, she married into the famous Ford (cars) family in 1947, when she wed William Clay Ford. The Fords became majority owners of the Lions in 1963, and Firestone Ford became principal owner following the death of her husband in 2014 at age 88. Firestone Ford remained principal owner until 2020, when she passed the baton to daughter Sheila Ford Hamp. But Firestone Ford remained heavily involved with the team, regularly attended practices and games. She attended a game at Ford Field as recently as this month. Jones, who bought the Cowboys in 1989, called Firestone Ford a heavily involved owner. "With all of that legacy, here she is, so sensitive, so involved in what we're doing in the NFL. She was great. She attended most of the meetings that I've attended over the last 30 years," Jones said on "Good Morning Football" on Wednesday. "And it was just an inspiration to see that beautiful lady on the other side of the room. I was a real admirer of her, and we're going to miss her." "I'll never forget her." Jerry Jones reflects on Martha Firestone Ford's lasting legacy and the impact she made on the Detroit Lions organization ❤️ pic.twitter.com/wyjifvEHf9 — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) November 25, 2026 All of the NFL's teams put out statements of condolences following Firestone Ford's death, as did Detroit mayor Mary Sheffield and governor-elect Jocelyn Benson. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and wife Jane also paid tribute in a statement Tuesday. The Goodells said: "Martha was special. She cared so deeply about her family, the players, their fans, and the city of Detroit. She was committed to making the Lions — and the game of football — better. Martha and her husband, William Clay Ford, led the franchise with dignity and integrity. We will miss her kindness and sweet sense of humor." item.title: Fisilau starts as England change five for All Blacks rematch
item.description: Greg Fisilau has made impressive replacement appearances over the past three weekends [Getty Images] Hard-hitting back row Greg Fisilau will make his first England start in one of five changes to their XV to face New Zealand. The Plymouth-born 23-year-old, whose father Keni was a Tonga international, has impressed off the bench in each of England's previous three wins this autumn. He brings an industrious carrying option to a back row that relies heavily on Ben Earl in that aspect of the game. Ben Curry's breakdown skills have been sacrificed to make space, with the Sale man relegated to the bench. Exeter's Fisilau has carried more than any other player in the Prem this season, as well as sitting fourth in the top-flight's tackle standings. Elsewhere Freddie Steward's good form is rewarded with a start ahead of George Furbank at full-back, while Tommy Freeman returns on the wing for Saturday's rematch (16:40 GMT). Freeman missed last weekend's 37-12 victory over the All Blacks with a minor thigh issue which forced his withdrawal in the hours before kick-off. Ellis Genge comes into the starting front row after a string of barnstorming performances across the latter half of England's Nations Championship campaign. He is joined in the front row by Luke Cowan-Dickie, who is preferred at hooker to Jamie George. Northampton's 21-year-old scrum-half Archie McParland, who made his debut off the bench against Japan a fortnight ago, is among the replacements once again. With less than a year until the Rugby World Cup, England head coach Steve Borthwick's auditions for fringe squad members are taking on more importance. Victory would ensure an autumn clean sweep, a sixth win in succession and a third-place finish in the overall standings of the inaugural Nations Championship. A win would also contribute to the northern hemisphere's points tally in a Ryder Cup-style competition which runs throughout the three days of action at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham. The tournament is being held every other year between Rugby World Cups and British and Irish Lions tours in an attempt to bring more of a narrative to the Test calendar and draw in fans. Six Nations holders France and world champions South Africa will contest Sunday's grand final (16:40 GMT). item.title: A South Side Thanksgiving
item.description: We’re all thankful for Miguel Vargas and his ability to overcome adversity in his time with the Chicago White Sox. (And to be a great slugging duo with Munetaka Murakami!) | Getty Images Miguel Vargas gave White Sox fans something substantial to bring to the Thanksgiving table: A reminder that a player’s first impression does not have to become his final chapter. That is a sentiment worth sharing on the South Side this November. The White Sox finished 84-78, swept Houston in the Wild Card Series and pushed Cleveland to five games in the ALDS. The ending hurt. It should have. Caring enough about October baseball to be disappointed was itself something to appreciate. This Thanksgiving, I’m thankful for a team that gave us reasons to watch, reasons to argue and reasons to start sketching a 2027 lineup before the turkey was out of the oven. Gratitude still leaves room for expectations. Some of these players need to improve. Some might be elsewhere next season. Appreciating their contributions does not require promising everybody another seat. But this table has room for all 26 players on Chicago’s announced ALDS roster, minus new Colorado Rockie Davis Martin. Each gets a helping of thanks, some statistical stuffing and something to save room for next year. Miguel Vargas: A second helping of belief — The helping: I’m thankful that Vargas gave fans a reason to reconsider what they thought they knew. His combination of power and patience offers a useful model: damage matters, but so does declining a pitch you cannot damage. — The stuffing: 33 home runs and 101 walks. — Save room for pie: Another year of that discipline, with more opportunities to turn baserunners into runs. Munetaka Murakami: Something worth getting out of your seat for The helping: I’m thankful for the anticipation. A lineup needs players whose at-bats make you put down the remote, and Murakami supplied the power to demand that attention. The stuffing: 35 home runs in 127 games. Save room for pie: More contact without sacrificing the ability to change a game with one swing. His ceiling becomes considerably more interesting if fewer plate appearances end without a ball in play. Colson Montgomery: Power with unfinished business The helping: I’m thankful that Montgomery gives the White Sox a substantial offensive weapon at shortstop. His season also gives us a useful distinction: Appreciating what a young player can do while asking for more of what he still needs. The stuffing: 31 home runs, alongside 227 strikeouts. Save room for pie: Fewer empty swings. The power already earns a place at the table; improved contact could make the entire meal better. Chase Meidroth: Keeping the line moving The helping: I’m thankful for the player whose contribution does not require a towering fly ball. Meidroth’s production gives the lineup another way to function when its biggest swings miss. The stuffing: A .276 average and 156 hits. item.title: Aaron Rodgers requested Mike McCarthy be removed from relaying plays
item.description: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Pieces of the puzzle are coming together around the Steelers’ shocking decision to bench Aaron Rodgers. The Steelers released a statement, through their team spokesman Burt Lauten, that Mason Rudolph will start against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday. Rodgers won’t even dress and is already announced as inactive. NFL insider Mike Garafolo said on NFL Network that the Steelers were in the process of changing the delivery of their play calling duties to quarterbacks coach Tom Arth. “There was going to be a change in the process this week,” Garafolo said. “Tom Arth is the quarterbacks coach. He was going to be the one to radio the plays in to Rodgers. That change was that this was going to be how things were going to go for the entire game,” Garafolo said. “They worked through that at practice yesterday. They were also having meetings as late as 5:30- 6 o’clock to figure this stuff out.” “Rodgers was the one that wanted this change to be made and that’s why it was happening as early as the walkthrough yesterday,” Garafolo said. Rodgers took first-team reps on Tuesday and met with the media like any typical week. What happened between Rodgers talking and 11:10 p.m. Tuesday night? “Nobody was talking about Rodgers being benched so I do believe that it was late last night when Mike McCarthy finally made the decision to bench Aaron Rodgers,” Garafolo said. “The question is, why?” Arth was the Steelers quarterbacks coach in 2025 when Rodgers joined the Steelers and was the only assistant coach to stay on staff when Mike McCarthy took over. item.title: AFC North’s changing of the guard from Steelers/Ravens to Bengals/Browns happening fast
item.description: For years- really, decades- the AFC North has seen the Cleveland Browns in the basement, with the Baltimore Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers running the show. The Cincinnati Bengals have had windows of time when they join the top two, but they haven’t had the kind of consistency that the others have. The Browns have been consistently bad, with just a couple of playoff appearances and no AFC North titles . Things have started to change during the 2026 NFL season, with Cincinnati and Cleveland at the top of the division, even if Pittsburgh had the same 6-4 record as the second-place team. Baltimore has fallen off without Lamar Jackson . Now, with the news of the Steelers benching Aaron Rodgers late on Tuesday night, after he practiced as the team’s starter the first two days of the week, the bloom seems to be off in Mike McCarthy’s first year. As our Producer at Behind the Steel Curtain said, Pittsburgh needs to reset everything in order to rebuild: It’s easy to say now, but they should have gotten rid of all the Tomlin guys. They were always going to have that “well Mike T wouldn’t have done this” about them. It’s a spoiled group. https://t.co/Q8MtftMykE — Jarrett Bailey (@JBaileyNFL) November 25, 2026 The Ravens may be looking at a similar turnover with Jackson’s contract at a point where the team either needs to try to extend him (something they’ve tried and failed to do), trade him, or release him this offseason. Given Jackson’s price tag, injury history, and limited playoff success, Baltimore’s future may not include their MVP-winning quarterback. There are many around Baltimore and Pittsburgh’s fanbases who are hoping that Jesse Minter and McCarthy are one-and-done coaches, whereas Cincinnati’s Zac Taylor was the one holdover in the division, and Todd Monken has had a positive start to his tenure in Cleveland. With the Bengals having stability at quarterback, an offensive line coming together well, great weapons on offense, and a defense coming together well, Cincinnati might be the cream of the crop in the AFC North for a few seasons. The Browns could be close behind, with a young, exciting roster of talented players all over the roster, extra draft picks over the next couple of years, and a coach who is making everything work ahead of schedule. By the time the next decade starts, we could be looking back at the 2026 NFL season as the time that the changing of the guard in the AFC North was fast-tracked, with the State of Ohio on top for a number of years. item.title: Eagles’ offensive changes produced less than encouraging results
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 22: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni looks on during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburg Steelers on November 22nd, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The more things change, the more they stay the same. The Philadelphia Eagles made notable changes to their offense in Sunday’s win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Less play-action, more pistol. They changed up the basis of Sean Mannion’s offense, as 84% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps were in the shotgun and 64.2% involved motion — both were season-highs. A season-high 42% of plays were snapped between six and 10 seconds left on the play clock — far above the previous high of 24.2%. Play-action percentage — the basis of Mannion’s offense — was 8.0%. That’s the lowest since Week 1 (5.7%). Shotgun play-action percentage was 14.3%, the highest since Week 1 (14.3%). The Eagles ran “11 personnel” 82.0% of the time, the second-highest percentage in a game this season (Week 6 vs. Panthers, 83.6%). “12 personnel” was 12.0%, the second-lowest percentage this year (Week 9 vs. Giants, 9.1%). The Eagles didn’t run “13 personnel” — three tight ends on the field — at all (despite having five tight ends on the active roster). There were significant changes on how the Eagles ran their offense, from pre-snap motion, to when they snapped the ball, and the formations they used. Since Joe Milton became the starting quarterback, the Eagles were trending in this direction. The results, unfortunately, have been more of the same. The Eagles can’t control the clock, they’ve been unable to stay on the field, and struggle to score points. This was with Saquon Barkley healthier (for a half at least) and DeVonta Smith back. Sean Mannion’s offense still failed to score 20 points and gain 250 yards. This was with the changes made — and how Philadelphia has been trending in that direction — over the last two weeks. There have been some positives with the changes, but the results have been what we’re accustomed to. Final three quarters were abysmal for an NFL offense When looking at the offensive numbers after the first quarter, it’s impressive the Eagles actually won the football game and snapped their losing streak. This also demonstrates how inept the Pittsburgh Steelers offense was on Sunday (or how well the Eagles defense played). The Eagles had 86 yards of total offense over the final three quarters on 36 plays — an average of 2.4 yards per play. On their nine drives, the Eagles averaged 10.8 yards per drive and 0.75 points per possession. The 3-and-out percentage was 50% (the Eagles lead the NFL in 3-and-out percentage). They had zero explosive plays while running 83.3% of the plays in shotgun and 60.5% of plays in motion. item.title: Colin Cowherd names two unsung heroes who have ‘changed everything’ for the Kansas City Chiefs
item.description: Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images Colin Cowherd believes two relatively unheralded players have transformed the Kansas City Chiefs. Neither Emmett Johnson nor Josh Downs arrived in Kansas City as established superstars, but both have made an immediate impact. Johnson was selected in the fifth round of this year’s NFL Draft and initially found himself behind Kenneth Walker in the running back pecking order. However, Walker has missed the last two games, allowing the rookie to step into a much bigger role and rush for 101 and 105 yards. His performances prove he can potentially handle the responsibility of a starting running back. Meanwhile, Downs arrived in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts , whereby the Chiefs sent a fourth- and fifth-round pick to strengthen their receiving corps. He has recorded 53 and 59 receiving yards in his first two games respectively for Kansas City, giving Patrick Mahomes another reliable target. Cowherd believes the pair have helped turn Kansas City into a much more complete team. He said: “I think Emmett Johnson and Josh Downs are the real deal. I think Emmett Johnson and Josh Downs have just changed everything. Over the last four games, they lead the NFL in passing yards and passing touchdowns. They’re not getting sacked. “They haven’t faced a very good schedule, and it gets significantly tougher, but they have a lot of these boxes checked: ace head coach, great DC, great quarterback, tremendous red-zone defense, long-ball threat. item.title: Real Madrid target Champions League top spot and €23 million windfall after perfect start
item.description: Real Madrid target Champions League top spot and €23 million windfall after perfect start Following their 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday , Real Madrid have collected all 15 points from their opening five UEFA Champions League matches this season. As such, Los Blancos are now within touching distance of their first major objective: securing a place in the top eight and avoiding the additional knockout play-off round. Now, according to AS , with three league-phase fixtures remaining, Jose Mourinho’s side are also chasing a potential financial reward worth almost €23 million. Direct qualification to Round of 16 the main objective Five victories have put Real Madrid at the top of the league phase standings, although their position remains subject to PSG’s result later today. Nonetheless, the perfect start has placed them in a strong position to reach the Last 16 directly. However, it must be noted that previous editions of the competition have shown that 15 points are not necessarily enough to finish inside the top eight. Five wins in five games for Real Madrid in the Champions League. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) But, 16 points have proved sufficient to secure a place in the top eight, giving Real Madrid three more opportunities to reach the required total and potentially finish even higher. For Mourinho and his men, direct qualification for the Round of 16 would also mean avoiding an extra knockout tie in the midst of an already packed schedule. Since the new format was introduced, Real Madrid have failed to secure a top-eight finish and the Portuguese tactician remains determined to turn that around. Almost €23 million in additional prize money at stake There is also a substantial financial incentive attached to finishing at the top of the league phase standings for Real Madrid. The Merengues have already earned €10.5 million from their five victories, with UEFA awarding €2.1 million for each win. That comes on top of the €18.6 million guaranteed for participating in the league phase, taking the club’s current earnings in the competition to €29.1 million. Securing top spot would help the club rake in €23 million. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Finishing first would bring further rewards. UEFA’s distribution includes €275,000 for each position in the final league-phase ranking, meaning the team finishing at the top would receive €9.9 million. A further €2 million is awarded for finishing inside the top eight, while qualification for the round of 16 brings another €11 million. Combined, those potential payments amount to almost €23 million. Real Madrid have three matches left in their league-phase campaign, beginning with the trip to London to face Arsenal on 9 December. They will then return to the Bernabeu on 19 January to take on Austrian side LASK Linz before travelling back to London on 27 January to face Shakhtar Donetsk at Stamford Bridge.

item.description: ‘We need to learn to enjoy moments like these’ – Martin Demichelis on RB Leipzig’s latest win RB Leipzig secured a 3-1 win against RC Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday night. Speaking after the game, head coach Martin Demichelis said the team still has issues to address despite the strong start. “We got off to a really good start. After ten minutes, we’d scored twice and had plenty of shots and corners. We played very well right up until half-time. We weren’t as good in the second half as we had been in the first,” he stated, further adding that the team lacked confidence on the ball and made a lot of mistakes: “Lens changed their approach and were the better side. There are things we need to address.” Demichelis also discussed the importance of enjoying the win: “We need to learn to enjoy moments like these. I congratulated the boys and told them that tonight wasn’t the time to be disappointed or have doubts. We can enjoy this win tonight,” he added. Regarding possible fatigue, he said they will try to utilize rotation going forward, even though that is not the issue at the moment: “That wasn’t our problem today, but fatigue will start to become a factor over the next few games. We’ll try to manage that by rotating the squad and sharing out the playing time. We need everyone in the squad.” Leipzig will travel to Old Trafford to face Manchester United in their next Champions League game but before that, they have important Bundesliga games against Freiburg and Mainz, while they will face Bayer Leverkusen in the DFB Pokal. item.description: Christchurch pitch for India vs NZ 2nd Test: Will bowlers get assistance from the Hagley Oval wicket or will it be another flat deck? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Pace bowlers have taken around 90 per cent of all Test wickets at Hagley Oval. Jacob Oram expects more bounce and movement in Christchurch than the Basin Reserve offered. Matt Henry says New Zealand will not try to predict the surface in advance. What Jacob Oram and Matt Henry expect from the Hagley Oval pitch in Christchurch The first Test of this series produced 1,327 runs for the loss of 24 wickets across five days, which is not the ratio either attack travelled to New Zealand expecting. Christchurch is supposed to be where that changes. Jacob Oram, New Zealand's bowling coach, made clear what the hosts are after when he spoke to reporters at the ground on Wednesday. "We're hoping that there's obviously a little bit more bounce and movement than we saw in Wellington," he said. He also warned against reading too much into the grass that will be left on the surface, which at Hagley Oval tends to look more threatening than it plays. Oram pointed out that it can dry out quickly once the match is under way. "It looks tough to start, but if you can get over that hump, then the batting becomes easier," Oram said, adding that New Zealand would not settle on their bowling plans until the morning of the match. Matt Henry struck a similar note at his own press conference in Christchurch, refusing to commit to any forecast of how the pitch will behave. "We don't have a crystal ball, so we don't know what it's going to be like," he said. The weather may decide it. Christchurch is forecast to be hot through the Test, which historically accelerates the drying process and flattens the surface out as the match goes on. MORE: New Zealand vs. India 2nd Test prediction, lineups and Hagley Oval pitch report — Who will win? Why Hagley Oval's Test record favours bowlers more than the Basin Reserve did The numbers support Oram's optimism. Teams bowling first have won 10 Tests at Hagley Oval against four for sides batting first, which is the most lopsided split at any New Zealand venue and explains why the toss carries unusual weight here. Spin barely features. Pace bowlers account for roughly 90 percent of the wickets taken at the ground, with slow bowlers averaging around three wickets a Test, and that is before the breeze off the Southern Alps is taken into account. item.description: Phillies lose polarizing free agent infielder to Royals on $20 million deal originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Phillies have been running it back for the last three years, and it's progressively gotten worse with each passing season. During the 2026-2027 MLB offseason, Dave Dombrowski and the Phillies know they need to make some changes, mainly to the starting lineup. While they've yet to make an addition, one change has already come to pass. According to Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic , the Kansas City Royals have reportedly agreed to a $20 million contract with free agent infielder Alec Bohm. His polarizing tenure in Philadelphia is now over, as he's headed to the AL Central this offseason. Phillies lose Alec Bohm to Royals with $20M reported deal "Free-agent third baseman Alec Bohm in agreement with Royals on a two-year, $20M contract, pending physical, source tells @TheAthletic," Rosenthal reported. While this isn't a roster move the Phillies are making this offseason, it's a very notable reported signing, as it means Bohm will officially not be coming back to Philadelphia in 2027. After spending the first seven years of his MLB career with the franchise, featuring some wild ups and downs, the Phillies and Bohm are headed different ways. Thanks to the Royals trading away Maikel Garcia, they needed infield help. While Bohm isn't of the same caliber as some of the other top options available this offseason, he's a solid veteran right-handed hitter who would be a nice pickup for a team. MORE : Blue Jays miss out on another premier free agent with Mets' Tarik Skubal news The Phillies had been trying to trade Bohm for two years before he left in free agency this offseason, but they couldn't find any takers. Now, he's joining the Royals, leaving the Phillies behind. A return to Philadelphia never seemed likely, not after the trade rumors over the past few years. But after the Phillies missed out on Teruaki Sato, there might've seemed to be a chance for the Phillies to turn back to their veteran infielder. Now, that's no longer possible, as Bohm is reportedly signing on with the Royals for $20 million over two years to likely fill in as their third baseman. Bohm posted 4.9 bWAR in seven seasons across 874 games played with 894 hits, 85 home runs, 483 RBI, and a 101 OPS+ to go with an All-Star nod and even a strong Home Run Derby run. It wasn't a perfect tenure in Philadelphia, and there were plenty of good and bad moments. As Bohm leaves the Phillies with a complicated legacy, the two sides are looking to the future without one another. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
